Historical_Significance: Adi Shankaracharya attained Mahasamadhi here in the 8th century CE; current monumental stone shrine built in 8th-9th century CE.

Founder: Pandavas (Traditional) / Adi Shankaracharya (Historic Restoration)

Religious_Significance: Chandra (Moon God) was cured of his wasting curse by Lord Shiva after intense penance here; praised in Rigveda.
Historical_Significance: Rebuilt by Sardar Patel following his Diwali 1947 pledge; consecrated by India's first President Dr. Rajendra Prasad on May 11, 1951.

Religious_Significance: Capital city founded by Lord Krishna after leaving Mathura; pilgrimage brings liberation from the cycle of rebirth.
Historical_Significance: Originally established by Krishna's great-grandson Vajranabha; present 16th-century temple incorporates 12th-century Chaulukya stone foundations; Adi Shankara established the Western Sharada Peetham here.

Constructed with stone slabs and marble, topped with a distinctive red spire (Shikhara) and a goose (Hamsa) motif. The floor and inner walls are embedded with silver coins donated by devotees.
Why_Famous: Only major temple dedicated to Lord Brahma in the world, red shikhara with Hamsa bird, sacred Pushkar Lake bath, annual world-famous Pushkar Camel Fair (Kartik Mela).
Religious_Significance: Pushkar is hailed as Tirtharaj (King of all pilgrimage centers); Lord Brahma dropped a lotus petal here to create the lake and performed a grand Vedic Yajna.
Historical_Significance: Traditional origin dating to 14th century CE; consecrated by Sage Vishwamitra; renovated by Maharaja Jawat Raj of Marwar in 1809 CE.

Temple_Name_Local: श्री महाकालेश्वर ज्योतिर्लिंग मंदिर उज्जैन मध्य प्रदेश
Alternate_Name: Mahakal Ujjain; Dakshinavarti Jyotirlinga; Mahakal Lok
Temple_Type: Dakshinavarti Jyotirlinga (3rd) / Sapta Puri / Kumbh Mela Tirtha
Main_Deity: Lord Shiva as Mahakaleshwar (The Lord of Time and Death - facing South / Dakshinavarti)
Secondary_Deities: Omkareshwar (first floor), Nagchandreshwar (third floor, open only on Nag Panchami), Vriddha Mahakal
Temple_Description: One of the twelve sacred Jyotirlingas, revered as the sole Dakshinavarti (south-facing) Jyotirlinga, positioned at the prime meridian of ancient Indian astronomy. Renowned worldwide for the daily pre-dawn 'Bhasma Aarti' where the deity is worshipped with sacred cow-dung ash (vibhuti). The newly inaugurated 900-meter Mahakal Lok Corridor features 108 grand sculpted pillars depicting Lord Shiva's Anand Tandav.
Why_Famous: Sole south-facing Jyotirlinga, pre-dawn Bhasma Aarti (04:00 AM), Nagchandreshwar temple (opened once a year on Nag Panchami), Mahakal Lok Corridor with 108 Shiv Stambhas and mural plazas.
Religious_Significance: Ujjain is one of the seven Mokshadayani Sapta Puris; Mahakal is the celestial king and protector of the city.
Historical_Significance: Mentioned in Kalidasa's Meghaduta; rebuilt by General Ranoji Shinde of the Maratha Scindia dynasty in 1734 CE; Mahakal Lok Corridor opened in 2022.
Construction_Period: Ancient origin; present structure 1734 CE; Mahakal Lok 2022 CE
Founder: Ranoji Shinde (Scindia Dynasty) / Government of Madhya Pradesh
Dynasty: Avanti / Scindia of Gwalior / Modern MP Government

Temple_Description: One of the 51 sacred Shakti Peethas where the tooth (Daant) of Goddess Sati fell. Consecrated at the sacred holy confluence of Shankhini and Dankini rivers. Revered as the sovereign deity and Kuldevi of the royal family of Bastar and over 30 indigenous tribal communities who bring their local village deities (Angas and Chhatras) during Bastar Dussehra.
Why_Famous: Tooth of Goddess Sati (Shakti Peeth), Bastar Dussehra (75-day festival - world's longest), unique amalgamation of tribal folk and Vedic rituals, Garuda pillar.
Religious_Significance: Supreme spiritual guardian of the entire Dandakaranya forest region; sacred confluence of black Shankhini and white Dankini waters.
Historical_Significance: Constructed in the 14th century CE by Maharaja Annama Deva, brother of Kakatiya King Prataparudra of Warangal, after migrating to Bastar in 1323 CE.
Architectural_Style: Kakatiya & Indigenous Bastar Wooden-Roof Stone Architecture
Founder: Maharaja Annama Deva (First King of Bastar Kakatiya Dynasty)

Temple_Description: One of the largest, most famous, and prominent Hindu temples in Goa. Famous for its magnificent seven-storey octagonal Deepastambha (lamp tower) which illuminates the entire courtyard when lit with hundreds of oil lamps. Features a distinctive blend of Goan Hindu, Maratha, and Indo-Portuguese architectural styles with pristine blue and white domes.

Religious_Significance: Principal Kuladevata (family deity) of many Saraswat Brahmin families across India.
Historical_Significance: Original temple was in Cortalim (Kushasthali); shifted secretly by night to Priol in 1560 CE to escape Portuguese Inquisition destruction; rebuilt by Marathas in 18th c. CE.

Historical_Significance: Present monumental temple initiated by King Anantavarman Chodaganga Deva in 1135 CE and completed by Anangabhima Deva III of Eastern Ganga Dynasty; visited by Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu who lived 24 years here.

Secondary_Deities: Three chlorite stone images of Surya catching morning, noon, and sunset rays
Temple_Description: A monumental 13th-century architectural masterpiece conceived as a colossal chariot of the Sun God Surya, featuring 24 intricately carved stone wheels (3.7 metres in diameter) serving as precise sundials, pulled by seven galloping stone horses. Inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage list in 1984 as a pinnacle of Kalinga stone sculpture.
Why_Famous: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1984), 24 sundial chariot wheels that calculate time to the second, erotic Mithuna sculptures, Natya Mandap with 128 dancing poses, annual Konark Dance Festival.
Religious_Significance: Mentioned in the Bhavishya Purana and Samba Purana as the sacred Arka Kshetra where Samba, son of Lord Krishna, was cured of leprosy by worshipping the Sun God.
Historical_Significance: Built around 1250 CE by King Narasimhadeva I of the Eastern Ganga Dynasty to commemorate his military victories; European sailors called it the 'Black Pagoda'.
Architectural_Style: Kalinga Style (Gigantic Chariot Pidha Deula in Khondalite stone)
Founder: King Narasimhadeva I (Eastern Ganga Dynasty; Chief Architect: Bisu Maharana)

Alternate_Name: Bhavatarini Temple; Dakshineswar Mandir; Sri Ramakrishna Sthalam
Temple_Type: Navaratna Nine-Spire Architectural Masterpiece / Siddha Shakti Sthal
Address: Dakshineswar, Kolkata, North 24 Parganas, West Bengal

Temple_Description: Located on the eastern bank of the holy Hooghly (Ganga) River. Built by philanthropist Rani Rashmoni in 1855 CE. World-renowned as the spiritual seat where mystic saint Sri Ramakrishna Paramahamsa served as priest and achieved God-realization across all major world faiths. Features the grand three-storey Navaratna (nine-spire) temple, twelve identical Shiva temples along the riverbank, and the sacred Panchavati grove.
Why_Famous: Spiritual abode of Sri Ramakrishna Paramahamsa, Rani Rashmoni's vision, 12 riverside Shiva temples (Dwadash Shiva), Panchavati meditation grove, Navaratna Bengal temple architecture, skywalk from metro.
Religious_Significance: Bhavatarini means 'She who liberates her devotees from the ocean of worldly existence (Samsara)'; birthplace of the modern Ramakrishna-Vivekananda renaissance.
Historical_Significance: Consecrated on Snana Yatra day, May 31, 1855 by Rani Rashmoni; Swami Vivekananda was introduced to Ramakrishna here in 1881.
Founder: Rani Rashmoni (Philanthropist and Zamindar of Janbazar)

Alternate_Name: Gaya Dham; Footprint of Lord Vishnu; Pitru Tirtha Gaya
Temple_Type: Historic Pitru Moksha Tirtha / Footprint of Vishnu Shrine
Address: Vishnupad Road, Chand Chaura, Gaya, Bihar
Main_Deity: Dharmasila (40-cm imprint of Lord Vishnu's sacred footprint in solid basalt rock)
Secondary_Deities: Lord Gadadhara, Narasimha, Ganesha, Shiva, Falgu River deities
Temple_Description: Located on the bank of the holy Falgu River in Gaya. The sanctum enshrines the 40-centimetre footprint of Lord Vishnu stamped into solid basalt rock (Dharmasila), enclosed in an octagonal silver-plated basin. Lord Vishnu placed his holy foot on demon Gayasura who offered his body for cosmic sacrifice. World-famous for the Pitru Paksha Shraddha pilgrimage where millions offer Pinda Daan for the salvation of ancestors.
Why_Famous: Footprint of Lord Vishnu (40 cm) stamped into solid rock, Pitru Paksha Pinda Daan pilgrimage, 30-metre octagonal grey granite Shikhara built by Maharani Ahilyabai Holkar in 1787, holy Falgu River.
Religious_Significance: Mentioned in the Ramayana where Lord Rama and Sita performed Pinda Daan for King Dasharatha; offering Pinda Daan here guarantees liberation for seven generations of ancestors.
Historical_Significance: Reconstructed in 1787 CE by the legendary queen Maharani Ahilyabai Holkar of Indore using master stone carvers and grey granite imported from Patharkatti.
Construction_Period: Ancient origin; present temple rebuilt 1787 CE
Founder: Maharani Ahilyabai Holkar of Indore

Temple_Name_Local: बाबा बैद्यनाथ ज्योतिर्लिंग मंदिर देवघर झारखंड
Alternate_Name: Deoghar Baidyanath Dham; Ravana Jyotirlinga; Kamna Lingam
Temple_Type: Jyotirlinga (9th) & Shakti Peeth (Heart of Sati - Jayadurga)
Main_Deity: Lord Shiva as Baidyanath (The Divine Physician / Kamna Lingam)
Secondary_Deities: Maa Parvati (linked by sacred red silk ribbon / Gathbandhan to Shiva), 21 subsidiary temples including Maa Kali, Annapurna, Saraswati
Temple_Description: One of the twelve sacred Jyotirlingas and also recognized as a Shakti Peeth (where the heart of Sati fell). Enclosed in a fortified courtyard containing 22 temples. Famously linked by the 'Gathbandhan' sacred red silk cloth connecting the spires of Baidyanath and Parvati temples. Epicentre of the historic 108-km barefoot Shravani Mela Kanwar Yatra from Sultanganj.
Why_Famous: 9th Jyotirlinga, Shravani Mela (world's longest religious walk 108 km from Sultanganj to Deoghar), Punchshool (five-pronged trident) atop the spire, Gathbandhan sacred cloth connecting Shiva and Parvati domes.
Religious_Significance: Demon king Ravana performed severe penance cutting his ten heads to please Shiva; Shiva restored his heads like a physician (Vaidya), hence named Baidyanath.
Historical_Significance: Ancient origin; renovated in 1596 CE by Raja Puran Mal, ancestor of the Maharaja of Gidhaur; British East India Company records document administration from 1788 CE.
Architectural_Style: Nagara (Pyramidal 72-foot stone spire with Panchashoola pinnacle)
Construction_Period: Ancient origin; present temple complex built 1596 CE
Founder: Traditional: Ravana & Vishwakarma; Historic: Raja Puran Mal of Gidhaur

Alternate_Name: Kamakhya Temple Guwahati; Yoni Peeth; Nilachal Mahapitha
Temple_Type: Supreme Maha Shakti Peeth (Yoni of Sati) / Tantric Epicentre
Main_Deity: Goddess Kamakhya (Natural spring-fed cleft in the subterranean bedrock representing the Yoni of Sati)
Secondary_Deities: 10 Mahavidyas: Bhuvaneshwari, Bagalamukhi, Chhinnamasta, Tripura Sundari, Tara, Kali, Bhairavi, Dhumavati, Matangi, Kamala
Temple_Description: Perched atop the sacred Nilachal Hill overlooking the mighty Brahmaputra River. The supreme seat of Tantric Shaktism and the foremost of the 51 Shakti Peethas. The dark subterranean sanctum contains no sculpted idol; worship is offered to a natural fissure in the bedrock fed by an underground natural perennial spring. Features the unique Nilachal hybrid architectural style with a 16-sided beehive dome.
Why_Famous: Foremost of the 51 Shakti Peethas, Ambubachi Mela (annual fertility celebration of Mother Earth), natural spring-fed Yoni stone, 10 Mahavidya shrines on Nilachal Hill, Guwahati Passenger Ropeway across Brahmaputra.
Religious_Significance: Goddess Sati's creative womb and yoni fell here during Shiva's Rudra Tandava; celebrated in the Kalika Purana and Yogini Tantra.
Historical_Significance: Stone basements date to 8th-10th century Mlechha and Pala dynasties; destroyed during invasions and rebuilt in stone-and-brick by Koch King Nara Narayana and General Chilarai in 1565 CE.
Architectural_Style: Nilachal Style (Cruciform Base with 16-sided Beehive Bulbous Shikhara)
Construction_Period: 8th Century CE basements; rebuilt 1565 CE by Koch Dynasty
Founder: Koch King Nara Narayana & General Chilarai (Chief Architect: Chichila)
Dynasty: Koch Dynasty / Ahom Kings (Rudra Singha additions)

Special_Pooja: Kumari Puja (worship of pre-pubescent girls as living forms of the Goddess), Durga Puja Mahashtami, Ambubachi Puja

Temple_Name_Local: মা ত্রিপুরা সুন্দরী মন্দির উদয়পুর ত্রিপুরা

Temple_Type: 51 Maha Shakti Peeth (Right Foot of Sati) / Kurma Peeth
Main_Deity: Maa Tripura Sundari (Soroshi - 5-foot black Kasti stone idol in standing posture)
Secondary_Deities: Chhotoma (smaller idol of Goddess carried by royal army in war), Shiva
Temple_Description: One of the 51 sacred Shakti Peethas where the right foot of Goddess Sati fell. Constructed atop a hillock resembling the hump of a tortoise (Kurma Pristhakriti), hence celebrated as a Kurma Peeth. The holy temple pond, Kalyan Sagar, located right behind the temple, is home to sacred giant hillock turtles (Bostami / Black softshell turtles) and indigenous fishes protected by ancient royal edict.
Why_Famous: Right foot of Goddess Sati (Shakti Peeth), Kurma Peeth tortoise hump hillock, Kalyan Sagar holy lake with giant softshell tortoises, Diwali Matabari Mela.
Religious_Significance: Consecrated by Maharaja Dhanya Manikya in 1501 CE following a divine revelation; one of the holiest shrines in Eastern and North-Eastern India.
Historical_Significance: Stone inscription records King Dhanya Manikya constructing the brick temple in Saka era 1423 (1501 CE); repaired by Maharaja Rama Manikya in 1681 CE.
Architectural_Style: Char-Chala Bengal / Tripuri Terracotta Vaulted Roof Architecture
Founder: Maharaja Dhanya Manikya (Manikya Dynasty of Tripura)

Daily_Pooja: Mangal Aarti, Shringar, Chandi Path, Anna Bhog, Sandhya Aarti with drums and conch, Shayan

Religious_Significance: Lord Murugan is revered as the divine protector of the islands; pilgrims take Vow (Kavadi) during annual festivals.
Historical_Significance: Established in 1926 by Tamil workers brought during colonial construction of Cellular Jail and harbor infrastructure; rebuilt in grand Dravidian style in 1999.
